The video segment displays two screenshots of what appear to be Twitter posts or similar online content, presented side-by-side on a light blue background. The top of the screen features a red banner with the text "visit www.thepeoplesperson.com for more of the latest Man United transfer news" (English). Both screenshots are from "Swiss Ramble" (@SwissRamble). The left screenshot features a text block stating: "In the last 5 years, the 20 Premier League clubs have benefited from £1.9 bln net financing with most of the money coming from their owners £1,569m (81%) and another £366m (19%) sourced from banks. However, there is a big difference between business models at individual clubs." (English) Below this, a detailed table titled "Premier League Financing - laid 5 years" (English) lists various football clubs and their financing data, with specific figures for owner financing and external financing over five years. Some figures are highlighted in green, while Manchester United's figures are highlighted in red, indicating a net outflow. The right screenshot shows a text block summarizing total financing for clubs: "In terms of total financing, two clubs have received by far the most in the last 5 years, namely #THFC £521m and #CFC £433m, followed by #EFC £256m, #AVFC £224m and #FFC £186m. In stark contrast, #MUFC and #AFC had significant net cash outflows with £169m and £101m respectively." (English) Below this text, a bar chart titled "Premier League Financing last 5 years - total financing (£'m)" (English) visually represents these figures, with green bars for clubs receiving financing and red bars for clubs with net cash outflows, specifically Manchester United and Arsenal. Both screenshots are timestamped "6:48 AM - 14 Sep 2020 - Twitter for iPhone". Throughout the segment, an off-screen male voice references specific numbers from the displayed data, highlighting Chelsea's £433 million investment, Man City's £133 million, Liverpool's £57 million, and Manchester United's £169 million outflow.
